I am 53. I have worked these 15 mu in Quzhou since I was a boy. My father taught me, and now I watch my neighbors. If Old Wang buys more urea, I buy more too. Last year was okay. This year I will do the same.

Ten mu is for wheat and maize, one after the other. Five mu is for cotton — me and my wife can still handle that much.

For wheat: I sow the improved seed that everyone in the village uses. Before sowing, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer on each mu — the kind with three numbers on it, 15-15-15. When the wheat turns green after winter, I topdress with half a bag of urea, about 30 jin per mu. I know it costs money, but I would rather waste a little fertilizer than see thin ears. I irrigate three times from my well: once when the wheat wakes up, once when it shoots up, and once when the grain is filling. I pay the machine man for rotary tillage. Two pesticide sprays — one for weeds, and one more if I see bugs. If the weather is normal, I will get about 450 kg per mu.

For maize: As soon as the wheat is off in June, I plant hybrid seed. Everyone uses hybrid now — the ears are much fatter. I put one bag of compound down at planting, then when the plants are knee-high I spread 40 jin of urea per mu. Two irrigations, three if July is very dry. Two sprays. Rotary tillage after the wheat straw is chopped. I expect 550 kg per mu.

For cotton: I plough deep in spring because cotton roots need soft, deep soil. I use improved seed. Each mu gets one and a half bags of compound and 40 jin of urea. I water three times — at flowering, when the bolls set, and once more before they open. Cotton needs more medicine. I spray five times for bollworm and mites. I hope for 260 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Fertilizer, diesel for the pump, machine hire — it all costs real yuan. But if I cut back and lose yield, that is a disaster. So I do what I did last year, and I watch the neighbors. If they spend more, I spend more.
